A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SYMDIFF and provide readable main texts, equations, tables, and appendices. Material can be matched across revisions, including the score/flow-matching extension moved from Appendix D to Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation experiments on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs, including model-size, augmentation, and finetuning studies in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original molecular-generation results, computational-resource measurements, and finetuning experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C. Retained original results also qualify.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 corrects the reverse-loop endpoint from 1 to 2 before the separate final sampling kernel. The stochastic symmetrisation procedure, recursive construction, and training objective remain unchanged; Algorithms 3-4 document previously described components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate molecular generation on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs with explicit hydrogen atoms. The finetuning study remains on QM9, and the score/flow-matching extensions remain theoretical rather than additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds measured GeoLDM and MUDiff comparisons to QM9 computational-efficiency evaluation in Table 2; END has no measured resource results. Conversely, the GEOM-Drugs comparisons with DiT, DiT-Aug, and SymDiff-H in v1 Appendix C.3 disappear. The main molecular-quality baseline lists remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The main GEOM-Drugs configuration changes from 6.4M parameters and 40 epochs to 31.2M and 55 epochs. Reported QM9 settings also change, including the main learning rate from 1e-4 to 2e-4, symmetrisation-network configurations, and smaller denoiser depths from 12 to 10/8 layers. Efficiency reporting replaces iterations/second with seconds/epoch and adds vRAM. Revised settings do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 removes the additional-500-epoch QM9 study from v1 Appendix C.2.4 and the GEOM-Drugs scaling and DiT/Haar/augmentation analyses from C.3.2-C.3.4. QM9 size and augmentation comparisons remain, as does the pretrain-finetuning study. These removals substantially reduce supplementary experimental support.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three evaluation runs and retain the single-run qualification for GEOM-Drugs GeoLDM and EDM results. Neither adds seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: GEOM-Drugs Table 4 replaces SymDiff's NLL/stability/validity of -196.77/84.15%/95.99% with -301.21/86.16%/99.27% under changed model and training settings. v2 adds timing/memory measurements and removes GEOM ablation/scaling results, the longer-training QM9 result, and several size-study metric entries. QM9 Table 1 and the finetuning results retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: New Appendix D gives sufficient conditions for the surrogate objective to equal the ELBO—deterministic gamma or G-equivariant k—and argues about attainable ELBO values relative to these cases. The existing symmetrisation, density, augmentation, and score/flow-matching results remain; theorem renaming and the streamlined Appendix A.1 largely restate existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: stochastic symmetrisation enables flexible, scalable equivariant diffusion without intrinsically E(3)-equivariant network components, with benefits on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs. The claimed first application to generative modelling remains; removing some uses of 'novel' does not change its substance.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale for why expressive models can make the surrogate objective effective. It removes the comparison-fairness discussion, including v1's qualification that unsymmetrised DiT already outperformed EDM on GEOM-Drugs. The architectural-flexibility explanation and the limitation of finetuning only the symmetrisation component remain.

D1.justification: The documented reproduction recipe changes across both benchmarks: v2 adds a project-code URL, explicitly identifies retained EDM noise schedules/discretisation, and revises layer, head, width, and optimiser specifications. It also expands runtime/memory reporting and explains baseline code and hardware constraints. The PDFs establish these disclosures, not external repository availability.

R1.justification: The Deep Sets citation to Zaheer et al. (2017) and its bibliography entry are removed when Appendix B.2 is rewritten. The other cited works and the central positioning relative to intrinsic equivariance and deterministic symmetrisation remain.

P1.justification: Substantial editorial restructuring affects the background, symmetrisation explanation, experimental narrative, and appendices. v2 distinguishes stochastic from distributional invariance, presents the theorem before its intuition, rewrites Appendix A.1 and architecture descriptions, and reorganises experiments around efficiency and ablations. Appendix C is substantially condensed and a new objective discussion precedes the relocated extensions.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganised: v2 introduces a broader QM9 resource table and combines selected accuracy and efficiency metrics in Table 3, while removing several appendix tables. It also adds Algorithms 3-4 and simplifies the Appendix A.1 string diagrams. These are display changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves objective explanation, implementation documentation, and measured computational comparisons. However, it removes GEOM-Drugs scaling/augmentation controls and the associated fairness qualification while reporting better scores from a larger, longer-trained model. The added clarity and resource evidence coexist with weaker controlled support for attributing those gains to symmetrisation, leaving no reliably assessable net quality direction.
